thread:
Maria G: FYI staging alert — host CPU climbs to ~85% at ~600 rps for many short streaming calls, p50 decode latency +15ms.
Kevin H: logs?
Maria G: Attaching short flame snapshot: `host_parse->tokenize->writev` hot. Also seeing lots of tiny grpc frames.
Jade: saw this after the minibatch hint change last week; tiny-batches increased writev/syscall churn. :thinking_face: 
Dan: kernel-selection probe also flipped default to v2 for short seqs on that canary — could be a microkernel mismatch causing extra memcpy.
Maria G: flame shows lock contention in tokenizer pool threads. sample snippet:
```
# perf sample
parse_tokenize+0x34
tokenizer_worker::wait_for_job
writev_latency_spike
grpc_writev
```
Kevin H: KV cache hitrate ok? If we hit misses we do extra parse work.
Maria G: KV cache hit stable (~92%) but eviction spikes coincide with the CPU spike window.
Jade: option: move lightweight tokenization off-host into preparse sidecar — on beta that gave ~8% host CPU reduction for short requests.
Dan: sidecar adds a network hop; for sub-50-token streaming requests that hop might dominate. Could do hybrid: host does header/fast-prefix tokenization, sidecar handles full tokenize for long/complex inputs.
Kevin H: also try server-side coalescing of small grpc writes — aggregate 2-3 tiny frames into one writev to reduce syscall overhead.
Maria G: agreed. quick experiments plan:
- revert minibatch hint on canary
- enable writev-coalesce patch (dev branch)
- cap tokenizer pool size and measure queue latencies
Kevin H: I'll run a canary with writev-coalesce + tokenizer cap, tag=ingest-coalesce-7951.
Infra-bot: deploy started for ingest-coalesce-7951 to staging (build 0.29.4) :rocket:
Jade: if coalesce helps, follow up by rolling back kernel-selection for short seqs until heuristics tuned.
Dan: I'll add instrumentation: kv_eviction_rate vs parse_ops/sec and push a small grafana panel.
Maria G: created ticket INF-4723 with flame + perf traces, assigning to @kevin.h and @jade.
Kevin H: taking it. note: watch p99 tail — coalescing can lower avg but increase max latency if window too large.
Maria G: good point. we'll limit coalesce window to 4ms initially. :thumbsup:
Jade: I have a mini-harness that repros this pattern (many 20-50 token streaming requests). ping me for it.
Kevin H: please share link to harness.
Jade: https://git.internal/redwood/ingest/harnesses/short-streamer
Maria G: thanks — running canary now, will report back in ~2h with staging numbers.
